reason: Selected within-system budget sweep supports bounded replanning; combined registry/interface ablations cannot isolate natural-language invocation alone.

candidates.title: Sweep a bounded replanning budget before extending recovery
candidates.rule: For a tool-orchestration harness with execution verification, measure the success-versus-cost curve over a few replanning rounds instead of allowing open-ended retries.
candidates.finding: Within HEART, ToolBench pass rate rises from 47.6 at zero replans to 75.1 at three, then 75.3 at five. NESTFUL full accuracy rises from 0.15 to 0.44 and remains there.
models: HEART backend not established in inspected sections
candidates.conditions: A verifier evaluates execution and feeds failures into replanning; zero budget disables that loop.
candidates.limitations: The exact useful budget is system-specific and precise cost accounting is not established in the inspected sweep. Registry and Tool Primitives are removed together in another ablation, so it cannot prove the interface alone caused that result. Reported zero attack success is limited to selected attacks.
candidates.validation_test: Sweep retry budgets on representative tasks with final success, latency, calls, side effects and cost. Set stopping criteria from measured marginal gains rather than copying three as a universal threshold.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
